units.claim: The domain layer holds the entity models and the use-case interfaces and imports no other layer.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/domain/' AND NOT b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/domain/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator

units.claim: The application layer holds the use cases, ports, errors and validations, and depends only on domain (39 edges) plus the cross-cutting common folder.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/application/' AND b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/domain/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator

units.claim: The presentation layer holds the controllers, middlewares and responses, and imports application (47 edges) and domain (15 edges) but never infrastructure.

citations.quote: I'm using the name **"Presentation"** for this layer.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/presentation/' AND b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/application/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator

units.claim: The infrastructure layer holds the express, knex and repository implementations, the outer frameworks-and-drivers ring, and imports inward to application (28 edges) and domain (7 edges).

citations.quote: This folder (layer) is where we add everything related to external "**Frameworks and Drivers**". Here you can add the repositories, external frameworks, web and so on.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/infrastructure/' AND b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/application/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator

units.claim: The main layer holds the composition-root factories and may depend on every other layer (16 edges to presentation, 13 to application, 9 to infrastructure).

citations.quote: This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/main/' AND b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/presentation/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator

units.claim: Layers run domain, application, presentation, infrastructure, main from inner to outer; imports follow this order except 9 edges where infrastructure imports main, which the dependency rule forbids.

citations.quote: >The overriding rule that makes this architecture work is The Dependency Rule. This rule says that source code dependencies can only point inwards. Nothing in an inner circle can know anything at all about something in an outer circle. In particular, the name of something declared in an outer circle must not be mentioned by the code in the an inner circle. That includes, functions, classes. variables, or any other named software entity.

citations.query: MATCH (a:File)-[:IMPORTS]->(b:File) WHERE a.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/infrastructure/' AND b.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/main/' RETURN count(*) AS numerator, count(DISTINCT a) AS denominator
